cells.tense: Present tense — you're the one saying how it goes, and you're saying it now.
cells.verb: declaring the shape things are going to take
cells.place: where the frame gets set in the first place
cells.ask: Leave one corner of the frame open on purpose — a question you don't close, a part you say out loud you haven't figured out yet — and watch the whole thing hold more without getting any weaker.
cells.core:
You say how it goes, and it goes that way. Not because you push — because the shape you name is one people can actually work inside, and they can feel that. The declaring and the fit are happening together, which is the whole trick.

The next thing this is good for isn't more structure. It's room. A frame this sound can afford to hold more than one answer at a time, and can afford a few places where you say 'I don't know yet' and mean it.
cells.sheetLine: You name the shape, and it fits.

cells.tense: Future tense — you're laying down the shape of things that haven't arrived yet.
cells.verb: claiming how it's going to go before it's gone anywhere
cells.place: where order is supposed to come from
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've already decided the shape of and go down into it instead of across it — follow it until you reach the place where your understanding actually runs out — and let the frame you set afterward come from that floor, so that things make sense around you again instead of just being settled.
cells.core:
You're setting the frame for rooms you haven't walked into. Every open question is getting an answer in advance, every loose thing a slot, and the deciding is running ahead of the knowing. Somewhere out there is a mess you're bracing for, and you're building against it now.

It's costing the thing frames are for. A structure declared this early organizes your worry, not the situation — and people can tell when the shape was set for your sake rather than theirs.
cells.sheetLine: You're settling it before you've understood it.

cells.tense: Past tense — the moment to say how it goes came and went, and you're still standing where it was.
cells.verb: holding back the shape you'd give things
cells.place: where the frame would get set, if anyone set it
cells.ask: Don't try to make yourself declare anything. Instead, put your hands on one small thing and build it steadily, for a stretch of days, without announcing it — and let the saying-so come back on its own, the way it does when you know something from having made it, until things start making sense in your presence again.
cells.core:
You see the shape it could take and you're not naming it. The room stays loose, other people's half-orders fill the gap, and you go along with frameworks you can see the cracks in. Somewhere behind you is a time when claiming the shape went badly, and that time is still doing the deciding.

The seeing hasn't gone anywhere. It's the declaring that stopped — and a frame nobody says out loud doesn't organize anything.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape. You've stopped saying it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — you're already setting the frame, and calling it something else.
cells.verb: shaping how it goes without saying so
cells.place: the place order is actually coming from
cells.ask: Gather what's already grown from the shapes you set — count one arrangement people are living inside and trace it back to the moment you named it — and say 'I made that' about it once, so that when things make sense around you, you know why.
cells.core:
The way things are organized around you is mostly your doing. How the conversation gets framed, what counts as the plan, which order things go in — people fall into the shape you name, and you describe it as 'just how it is' or as someone else's call.

The structure is running on your say-so, and your say-so isn't getting the credit. That's not modesty doing it; it's a frame being set with the pen put down.
cells.sheetLine: You're already setting the frame. You just haven't claimed it.
